answer: In an agent marketplace trading goods from pearl jewelry and nectar to trellis kits, each seller identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before it can bid for jobs. Creating accounts is cheap, but activating 10,000 fake sellers ties up $1 million for a month. The bond applies separately to every identity, so splitting funds across accounts cannot evade the minimum, and the attacker pays the financing cost even if no fraud is detected.
